content:
Here's a comprehensive NCLEX preparation todo list:

## **Study Planning**
- [ ] Choose test date and register with Pearson VUE
- [ ] Create 6-8 week study schedule
- [ ] Set daily study goals (2-4 hours minimum)
- [ ] Schedule weekly practice tests

## **Study Resources**
- [ ] Get NCLEX prep book (Kaplan, Saunders, or ATI)
- [ ] Purchase UWorld question bank subscription
- [ ] Download NCLEX-RN app for mobile practice
- [ ] Join NCLEX study group or online forum

## **Content Review**
- [ ] Review all major systems:
  - [ ] Cardiovascular
  - [ ] Respiratory
  - [ ] Neurological
  - [ ] Musculoskeletal
  - [ ] Gastrointestinal
  - [ ] Renal/Urinary
  - [ ] Endocrine
  - [ ] Immune/Hematologic
- [ ] Master pharmacology categories
- [ ] Study lab values (memorize normal ranges)
- [ ] Review maternal/newborn nursing
- [ ] Study pediatric milestones
- [ ] Practice mental health concepts
- [ ] Review infection control procedures

## **Test-Taking Strategies**
- [ ] Learn Maslow's Hierarchy application
- [ ] Master ABC prioritization (Airway, Breathing, Circulation)
- [ ] Practice SATA questions (Select All That Apply)
- [ ] Study delegation principles (RN, LPN, UAP)
- [ ] Review safety protocols

## **Practice Questions**
- [ ] Complete 75-150 questions daily
- [ ] Review all rationales (right AND wrong)
- [ ] Keep error log of missed topics
- [ ] Take CAT-style practice exams weekly
- [ ] Aim for 60%+ on practice tests consistently

## **Final Week Preparation**
- [ ] Light review only - no new material
- [ ] Practice relaxation techniques
- [ ] Confirm test location and arrival time
- [ ] Prepare test day items (ID, ATT letter)
- [ ] Get adequate sleep (7-8 hours)
- [ ] Plan healthy meals

## **Test Day**
- [ ] Eat balanced breakfast
- [ ] Arrive 30 minutes early
- [ ] Use tutorial time to calm nerves
- [ ] Take breaks as needed
- [ ] Trust your preparation

Remember: Consistency is key! Focus on understanding concepts, not just memorization.
